intro:

body:
## Faisal Town Islamabad rental market

Faisal Town Phase 1 / F-18 has an active residential rental market.

Current property portals show full houses, upper portions, lower portions, flats and rooms available across the wider Faisal Town F-18 area.

For tenants looking specifically for a house, the most useful comparison is based on:

- block
- house size
- bedrooms
- furnished or unfurnished condition
- street location
- parking
- utilities
- house condition
- monthly rent
- security deposit
- lease terms

Rental inventory changes quickly, so use this page as a current-market guide rather than a fixed catalogue.

## Current house rents in Faisal Town F-18

Current asking rents vary considerably by size and condition.

Recent portal examples include:

- 5-marla houses around PKR 90,000 to PKR 100,000 per month
- 8-marla houses around PKR 110,000 to PKR 132,000 per month
- furnished 5- and 8-marla houses at materially higher rents
- upper portions at lower monthly rents than comparable full houses

These are current seller or landlord asking rents, not official rental rates or guaranteed final agreements.

A well-furnished or brand-new property can ask significantly more than an older unfurnished house of the same size.

## 5 marla houses for rent

5-marla houses are among the more common rental options in Faisal Town F-18.

Current listings include examples around the PKR 90,000 to PKR 100,000 monthly level, while furnished 5-marla houses can be considerably higher.

When comparing 5-marla houses, check:

- bedroom count
- number of kitchens
- parking
- independent or shared access
- furnishing
- gas availability
- electricity meter
- water arrangement
- house age
- block and street

Do not compare only the monthly rent.

A cheaper house may have weaker parking, older fixtures or utility limitations.

## 8 marla houses for rent

8-marla houses are also common in the Faisal Town F-18 rental market.

Recent listings include asking rents around PKR 110,000 to PKR 132,000 for unfurnished or brand-new examples, while furnished properties can be substantially more expensive.

An 8-marla house may suit a larger family because it commonly offers more bedrooms, living space and parking.

Always compare the exact layout rather than assuming every 8-marla house is similar.

## Furnished houses for rent

Furnished houses usually carry a noticeable rental premium.

A furnished property may include:

- beds
- sofas
- dining furniture
- curtains
- appliances
- air conditioners
- refrigerators
- kitchen equipment
- internet equipment
- security cameras

Before agreeing to a furnished rental, prepare a written inventory of included items and note their condition.

Take photos or video at handover.

This helps avoid disputes over missing or damaged fixtures when the tenancy ends.

## Full house vs upper or lower portion

Not every tenant needs a full house.

Faisal Town Phase 1 currently also has active upper- and lower-portion rental inventory. Current upper-portion listings include options in Blocks A, B and C. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

A portion may offer a lower monthly rent, but check:

- separate entrance
- separate electricity meter
- gas sharing
- water sharing
- parking allocation
- roof access
- privacy
- common areas
- maintenance responsibilities

A lower rent is not always better if utilities and access are heavily shared.

## Block A rental options

Block A has active house and portion rental inventory.

Current listings include full houses as well as upper portions. A dedicated Block A rental example is also currently listed in Phase 1. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

When comparing Block A properties, consider:

- street access
- road width
- proximity to commercial activity
- house age
- parking
- nearby construction
- family suitability

## Block B rental options

Block B also has active rental inventory.

A recent 8-marla double-storey house in Block B was listed around PKR 132,000 per month. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

Do not treat that as a standard Block B rent.

The exact amount depends on house condition, furnishing, bedrooms, location and landlord expectations.

## Block C rental options

Block C has active rental activity, including 5-marla houses and furnished homes.

Recent Block C listings include furnished and unfurnished 5-marla options. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

Block C may be relevant to tenants looking for smaller houses, but the exact street and house condition should still drive the decision.

## What affects rent in Faisal Town

Monthly rent is influenced by:

- block
- house size
- construction age
- furnishing
- bedrooms
- attached bathrooms
- double-unit layout
- parking
- corner or main-road position
- street condition
- utility availability
- security
- proximity to shops and services
- landlord flexibility
- lease duration

A newly built house can command materially more rent than an older house of the same size.

## Utilities to check before renting

Before paying a deposit, confirm:

- electricity meter
- meter reading
- gas availability or alternative arrangement
- water source
- water pressure
- backup water storage
- internet availability
- sewerage
- generator or solar system, if offered

If utilities are shared, get the billing method in writing.

Do not rely only on verbal assurances.

## Parking and access

Parking can be a major practical issue.

Confirm:

- how many cars can park inside
- whether street parking is practical
- whether another tenant shares the driveway
- gate width
- access for larger vehicles
- whether the street becomes congested

Visit the property during the time of day when you normally expect to arrive home.

## Rental deposit and advance rent

Before paying money, confirm the exact financial terms.

Ask for:

- monthly rent
- security deposit
- advance rent
- agency commission
- maintenance charges
- utility deposits
- possession date
- payment date each month
- refundable amount
- conditions for deduction

Do not send a deposit until you have verified the property and landlord or authorized representative.

## Verify the landlord

Ask to see evidence that the person renting the house has authority to do so.

Depending on the situation, check:

- owner identification
- ownership documentation
- authorized representative letter
- power of attorney where relevant
- property address
- rent agreement details

If an agent is involved, make sure payments are being made to the correct person and are properly receipted.

## Rental agreement checklist

A written rental agreement should clearly record:

- tenant and landlord names
- property address
- monthly rent
- deposit
- advance rent
- tenancy start date
- lease duration
- notice period
- annual rent increase, if agreed
- repair responsibilities
- utility responsibilities
- permitted use
- subletting conditions
- handover condition
- refund terms

Do not leave major financial terms to verbal understanding.

## House inspection before possession

Inspect the house carefully before signing or moving in.

Check:

- seepage
- roof leaks
- bathrooms
- plumbing
- electrical sockets
- air conditioners
- geysers
- kitchen fixtures
- doors and locks
- windows
- paint
- flooring
- water pressure
- parking gate
- appliances if furnished

Record existing defects in writing.

Take dated photos or video at handover.

## Family rental considerations

Families may also want to compare:

- nearby schools
- mosque access
- grocery and market access
- street noise
- privacy
- security
- children’s outdoor space
- parking
- commute

These practical factors may matter more than saving a small amount on monthly rent.

## Company or office-use inquiries

If a company or organization wants to rent a house, confirm that the landlord accepts the intended use.

Ask about:

- company lease
- staff occupancy
- office use
- visitor activity
- parking
- signage
- commercial restrictions
- tax or documentation requirements

Do not assume that every residential property can be used for business purposes.

## How to compare rental options

Create a simple shortlist using the same criteria for every property:

1. Block
2. House size
3. Bedrooms
4. Monthly rent
5. Deposit
6. Furnished or unfurnished
7. Parking
8. Utilities
9. House condition
10. Commute
11. Lease terms
12. Move-in date

This prevents a visually attractive house from appearing cheaper once deposits, utilities or repairs are considered.

## Before paying a rental deposit

Before paying:

1. Visit the house.
2. Verify the landlord or authorized representative.
3. Confirm the full address.
4. Agree monthly rent.
5. Agree deposit.
6. Agree advance rent.
7. Review the lease.
8. Check utilities.
9. Record fixtures.
10. Obtain a receipt.

If the landlord, agent and property details do not match, resolve the issue before transferring money.
